1.note: Alternate translation: [So Israel started the journey to Egypt with all his family members and belongings] or [So Israel and his family started traveling toward Egypt with all his belongings]

The author is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [he offered offerings] or [burned some of his animals on an altar there as sacrifices]
Alternate translation: [to God, whom his father Isaac had served]

2.q: וַ⁠יֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֤ים ׀ לְ⁠יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּ⁠מַרְאֹ֣ת הַ⁠לַּ֔יְלָה וַ⁠יֹּ֖אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֣ב ׀ יַעֲקֹ֑ב
2.note: God repeats Jacob’s name to communicate that he has something urgent or important to tell him. Make sure your translation of this phrase does not sound angry or critical. Also see how you translated **vision** in Genesis [15:1](ta:15).
For some languages, it is more natural to put this quotation margin (**he said**) after the quote. Alternate translation: [Jacob replied to him]

Consider again how you translated the idiom **Behold me** throughout the book of Genesis. See [22:1](ta:22), 7, 11; [27:1](ta:27), 18; 31:11; 37:13; 46:2. Alternate translation: [Here I am, Lord] or [Yes, Master?] or [I am listening, Lord]

3.note: See how you translated **the God of** in [verse 1](ta:46). Alternate translation: [I am God, the God whom your father served]
Alternate translation: [You must not be afraid]
Alternate translation: [to move down to the country of Egypt] or [to go to the country of Egypt and settle there]

See how you translated **I will make you into a great nation** (and similar phrases) in Genesis 12:2; 17:20; 18:18; 21:13, 18. Alternate translation: [because I will make you and your descendants] or [because I will make your family] or [because I will give you many descendants, who will]
Alternate translation: [multiply and become an important ethnic group there]

4.note: Consider what is the best way to translate the emphatic pronoun **I** here and in the next clause. Also see how you translated **down** and **up** in Genesis 45:9. Alternate translation: [I personally will go with you to Egypt]
The pronoun **you** refers here to Jacob’s descendants.

This clause refers to the custom of closing a person’s eyes after he died and means that Joseph would be with Jacob when he died. Alternate translation: [And when you die, Joseph will be right there to close your eyes]

5.note: Be consistent with how you spell **Beersheba** throughout the book of Genesis. See 21:14, 31–33; 22:19; 26:23, 33; 28:10; [46:1](ta:46), 5. Alternate translation: [So Jacob left the city of Beersheba] or [After that, Jacob whose other name was Israel left the city of Beersheba]

“and his sons, the sons of Israel, took/transported him their father” or “and his sons, that is the sons of Israel, took/transported him” or “and his sons took/transported him.” **Israel** is the name that God gave to Jacob (Genesis 32:28, 35:10). In [chapters 45](ta:45) and 46, the text repeatedly switches back and forth between both of Jacob’s names. Make sure it is clear in your translation that these two names refer to the same person. You could include a footnote that helps readers understand what is happening. Alternate translation: [and his sons, the sons of Israel, took him their father] or [and his sons, that is the sons of Israel, took him] or [and his sons transported him]
See how you translated “little ones and … wives” in Genesis 45:19. Alternate translation: [as well as their children and wives]
See how you translated **carts** in Genesis 45:19, 21, 27.
For a note about how **Pharaoh** is used like a name in the Bible, see 12:15. Alternate translation: [that Pharaoh the king of Egypt] or [that the king of Egypt]

The pronoun **him** refers to Jacob, the head of his family, and includes Jacob’s wives and children. It may be necessary to use the plural pronoun “them” to make that clear. Alternate translation: [to transport him to Egypt] or [for them to ride on to Egypt]

6.note: Alternate translation: [They also took with them their animals]

Consider again how you translated **possessions** in the book of Genesis. See 12:5 (and note); 13:6; 14:11–12, 16, 21; 15:14; 31:18; 36:7; 46:6. It may be necessary to translate this term in slightly different ways, depending on the context.
Consider again how you translated **acquired** in the book of Genesis. See 12:5; 31:18; 36:6; 46:6. Alternate translation: [that they had accumulated]

7.q: בָּנָ֞י⁠ו וּ⁠בְנֵ֤י בָנָי⁠ו֙ אִתּ֔⁠וֹ בְּנֹתָ֛י⁠ו וּ⁠בְנ֥וֹת בָּנָ֖י⁠ו
7.note: Consider what is the best way in your language to list these descendants. Alternate translation: [including his sons and grandsons, and his daughters and granddaughters] or [including his sons, daughters, grandsons, and granddaughters]

For some languages, it may be clearer or more natural to change the order of the clauses in this verse and say, “He/Jacob brought his entire extended family with him to Egypt, including his sons …” Alternate translation: [Yes, Jacob brought his entire family with him to Egypt] or [Jacob had all his descendants with him when he arrived in Egypt]

8.note: Some translations put verses 8–14, 16–17, and 19–24 in list format, beginning a new paragraph with each of Jacob’s sons.

9.note: Throughout this section (verses 9–27), some translations use a colon before each list of names instead of **were** or “who were.”

For some languages it is more natural to include **and** between every name in a list like this. For other languages it is more natural to use commas between names and leave **and** implied, except before the last name in the list. See how you translated similar lists of names in [Genesis 10](ta:10).

10.note: In this list, only Shaul had a Canaanite mother. See how you translated **Canaanite** in Genesis 38:2. Alternate translation: [and Shaul, whose mother was a Canaanite] or [and Shaul. (Shaul had a Canaanite mother.)]

12.note: Be consistent here with how you spelled these names in Genesis 38:3–11, 26, 29–30.
Alternate translation: [actually, Er and Onan had already died in the land of Canaan]
Alternate translation: [Perez had sons named Hezron and Hamul]

13.note: Numbers 26:24 and 1 Chronicles 7:1 have the same list of Issachar’s sons as here, but instead of **Puvah** and “Job,” they have “Puah” and “Jashub.” Some translations keep the spelling for these names the same in all three locations to avoid confusion. Alternate translation: [Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron]

Alternate translation: [of Leah and Jacob who were born]
Alternate translation: [in the land of Paddan Aram]

Alternate translation: [All together those sons, daughters and grandchildren totaled thirty-three persons]

16.note: This verse begins a new section in the list of Jacob’s descendants. Decide what is the best way to begin this new section in your language.

Alternate translation: [Beriah had sons named Heber and Malkiel]

18.q: וַ⁠תֵּ֤לֶד אֶת־אֵ֨לֶּה֙ לְ⁠יַעֲקֹ֔ב שֵׁ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה נָֽפֶשׁ
18.note: Consider whether it is better in your language to change the order of clauses in this verse and say, “Those were sixteen descendants that Jacob had with his concubine Zilpah, whom Laban had given to his daughter Leah as a maidservant/servant.” Alternate translation: [Zilpah and Jacob had those sixteen descendants] or [The total number of those descendants that Zilpah and Jacob had together was sixteen]

19.q: בְּנֵ֤י רָחֵל֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב יוֹסֵ֖ף וּ⁠בִנְיָמִֽן
19.note: This verse begins a new section in the list of Jacob’s descendants. Decide what is the best way to begin this new section in your language.

20.q: אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָֽלְדָה־לּ⁠וֹ֙ אָֽסְנַ֔ת בַּת־פּ֥וֹטִי פֶ֖רַע כֹּהֵ֣ן אֹ֑ן
20.note: See how you translated “Asenath … daughter of Potiphera the priest of On” in Genesis 41:45.

21.note: Remember to use (or not use) **and** between the names in this list in a way that is natural in your language.

22.note: Alternate translation: [All those were the descendants]

Alternate translation: [The total number of those descendants was fourteen]

23.note: This verse begins a new section in the list of Jacob’s descendants. See how you started verse 16, which is similar.

24.note: Consider again how you translated these lists of names in this chapter (verses 9–24).

25.note: Be consistent in how you spell **Bilhah** in the book of Genesis. See 29:29; 30:3–5, 7; 35:22, 25; 37:2; 46:25. Also see how you translated verse 18, which is similar in structure to verse 25. Alternate translation: [Those were the descendants of Jacob and Bilhah]
Alternate translation: [who was the servant woman whom Laban had given to his daughter Rachel]

For some languages it is better to change the order of clauses in this verse and say, “All those were seven descendants that Jacob had with his concubine Bilhah, whom Laban had given to his daughter Rachel as a maidservant/servant.” Alternate translation: [The total number of those descendants that Bilhah and Jacob had together was seven] or [Those descendants that Bilhah had with Jacob totaled seven persons]

26.note: Alternate translation: [The total number of people who traveled with Jacob to Egypt]

Make sure that your translation of this idiom can be read in public without offending or embarrassing listeners. See how you translated a similar idiom in Genesis 35:11. Alternate translation: [who came from him] or [who were his blood relatives] or [who were his biological descendants]
Alternate translation: [not including his wives or the wives of his sons]

For some languages it is clearer and more natural to change the order of the clauses in this sentence and say, “Altogether Jacob had sixty-six blood relatives who went with him to Egypt. That number does not include his wives or his sons’ wives.” Alternate translation: [was sixty-six people in all]

27.q: וּ⁠בְנֵ֥י יוֹסֵ֛ף אֲשֶׁר־יֻלַּד־ל֥⁠וֹ בְ⁠מִצְרַ֖יִם נֶ֣פֶשׁ שְׁנָ֑יִם

Alternate translation: [ahead of them to Joseph]
Alternate translation: [to find out which way to go] or [to ask him how to get]

Goshen was a region or territory that was part of the country of Egypt. For some languages it is better to make that explicit here, rather than wait until the end of the verse. Also be consistent here with how you spelled **Goshen** in Genesis 45:10. Alternate translation: [to the region of Goshen] or [to Goshen County]
Make sure it is clear in your translation who is being referred to here. Alternate translation: [Then Jacob and his family traveled to]
If you use **the land of Goshen** earlier in this verse, it may be better to just say **Goshen** here. Alternate translation: [the region of Goshen] or [Goshen County]

29.note: Joseph may have harnessed his horses to his chariot himself, or he may have had his servants do that for him (which was usual for a powerful person like him). Consider how you translated similar situations in Genesis 41:48. Also see how you translated **chariot** in Genesis 41:43. Alternate translation: [Then Joseph got his cart ready] or [Then Joseph had his servants get his cart ready]
See how you translated **went up** in Genesis [13:1](ta:13) and “go up” in Genesis 45:9.
Alternate translation: [When he got there, Joseph went up to his father]
See how you translated “fell on … neck” in Genesis 45:14. Alternate translation: [and put his arms around his neck] or [and hugged him strongly]

30.note: Alternate translation: [Then Israel exclaimed to him]

Jacob did not die until 17 years later (Genesis 47:28). Make sure your translation of this clause does not mean or imply that Jacob wanted to die soon or that he thought he would die soon. Alternate translation: [Now I will die happy]

In this context, **your face** refers to Joseph, not just his face. Decide what is the best way to communicate that in your language. Alternate translation: [since I have seen you face to face] or [since I have seen you in person]

31.note: Alternate translation: [Then Joseph told his brothers]
Make sure that the way Joseph refers to Pharaoh here sounds respectful in your translation. See what you did in Genesis 41:35. Alternate translation: [I will go to King Pharaoh and tell him]
Consider whether it is better in your language to translate this embedded quote (in verses 31–32) with a direct or indirect quote.
Alternate translation: [have come here from the land of Canaan to live near me]

32.note: Be consistent here with whether you are translating this embedded quote (that began in verse 31) as an direct or indirect quote. Alternate translation: [The men of my family tend sheep and goats] or [I will also tell him that you men in my family raise sheep and goats]
Alternate translation: [for they are livestock raisers]
Alternate translation: [as well as everything else]
Alternate translation: [that they have] or [that is theirs]

33.note: This phrase introduces and emphasizes what Joseph says next. Consider what is the best way to communicate that in your language.
Consider whether it is better in your language to translate this embedded quotation with a direct or indirect quote. Alternate translation: [summons you and asks you what your work is]

34.q: אַנְשֵׁ֨י מִקְנֶ֜ה הָי֤וּ עֲבָדֶ֨י⁠ךָ֙ מִ⁠נְּעוּרֵ֣י⁠נוּ וְ⁠עַד־עַ֔תָּה
34.note: The phrase “Your servants” shows respect to Pharaoh and acknowledges his high position. It does not mean that Pharaoh actually owns Joseph’s brothers as servants. Translate this in a polite way that shows respect toward Pharaoh. Alternate translation: [Your Majesty, we have raised livestock since the time we were young]
See how you translated **fathers** in Genesis 15:15. Alternate translation: [which is the same occupation that our forefathers had]
Alternate translation: [If you say that, then]

The idea here is that Jacob’s family would be permitted to live in rural areas to raise their livestock away from most Egyptians, who despised sheep herders. Alternate translation: [you will be allowed to live privately] or [he will permit you to live privately]
Alternate translation: [in the region of Goshen] or [in Goshen County]

For some languages it is clearer and more natural to change the order of phrases in this clause. Also see how you translated **abomination** in Genesis 43:32. Alternate translation: [sheep herders are detestable to Egyptians] or [the people of Egypt have disdain for sheep herders] or [Egyptians detest everyone who raises sheep]
